correctness.rationale: For unit approval ballots of size <=2 and any finite committee size, set selected losses a_c=1-x_c and unselected gains b_d=x_d, with equal sums by seat constraint. Ballots fully selected force losses zero; crossing doubletons impose b_d>=a_c. Threshold sets P_t and Q_t preserve weak improvements. Exchange lemma: |P_t|>|Q_t| permits padding the threshold committee to strict integral dominance, handling approved outside candidates in or out of Q. Thus for a PO W, |P_t|<=|Q_t| at all thresholds; equality of integrals makes these counts equal a.e. Layer-cake integration of utility gains then converts a strictly fractionally dominating x into a strictly improving size-k threshold committee, contradiction. Converse trivial. Boundary witness with ballots {acd,ace,ade,bc,bd,be,cd}, W={ab}, x=(0,1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2) checked against all ten integral two-seat alternatives: fractional dominance but no integral dominance.
